epithet: The siege of Madinah, and the Prophet’s ﷺ household
lede: Ten thousand men camped outside a city defended by a ditch, while inside it some whispered that Allah and His Messenger had promised nothing but a delusion. The surah of that winter — and of the laws that reshaped the Arab family, beginning in the Prophet’s ﷺ own house.

names.name: al-Aḥzāb
names.note: After the allied hosts — Quraysh, Ghaṭafān and those who joined them — who besieged Madinah in the fifth year. The same event is known as the Battle of the Trench, al-Khandaq.

revelation.detail: It is Madinan in the saying of all. Al-Qurṭubī notes its subject at the outset: it came down about the hypocrites and the hurt they did to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and their slanders about him and his marriages. Its events fall in the fifth year of the Hijrah — the siege in Shawwāl, the Banū Qurayẓah directly after, and the Prophet’s ﷺ marriage to Zaynab bint Jaḥsh in the same year. The traditional order places it ninetieth.
revelation.when: Madinah, the fifth year of the Hijrah: the Battle of the Trench and the months around it

evidence.quote: سُورَةُ الْأَحْزَابِ مَدَنِيَّةٌ فِي قَوْلِ جَمِيعِهِمْ. نَزَلَتْ فِي الْمُنَافِقِينَ وَإِيذَائِهِمْ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ، وَطَعْنِهِمْ فِيهِ وَفِي مُنَاكَحَتِهِ وَغَيْرِهَا. وهي ثلاث وَسَبْعُونَ آيَةً

setting: After the Banū al-Naḍīr were expelled from Madinah, some of their chiefs went from tribe to tribe raising an alliance to destroy Islam at its root. Quraysh came from the south under Abū Sufyān; Ghaṭafān and their allies from the east: some ten thousand men, against a city that could field three thousand. On the advice of Salmān the Persian, the Muslims dug a trench across the open northern approach — a device the Arabs had never met. The Prophet ﷺ dug with them, in the cold, with a stone tied against his stomach for hunger.

The siege lasted most of a month. Then the Banū Qurayẓah, the last Jewish tribe in the oasis, bound by treaty to its defence, went over to the enemy, and the city was open from behind. The surah records what that felt like: “when they came at you from above you and from below you, when eyes swerved and hearts reached the throats, and you thought thoughts about Allah. There the believers were tried, and shaken with a mighty shaking.” The hypocrites said aloud what they had been thinking, and began asking leave to go home.

No battle was fought. Allah sent against the confederates a bitter wind, and hosts they could not see; their tents were torn up and their fires put out, and they broke camp in the night. The Prophet ﷺ said: “Now we shall march on them, and they will not march on us.” He was told at once to go to the Banū Qurayẓah.

Woven through the account of the siege is a second subject: the Prophet’s ﷺ household, and through it the reform of the family. Adoption as the Arabs practised it — a man’s adopted son taking his name and counted his heir, his divorced wife forbidden to the adopter — is abolished: “Call them by their fathers.” Zayd, who had been called Zayd son of Muḥammad, became Zayd ibn Ḥārithah again; and when his marriage to Zaynab ended, the Prophet ﷺ was commanded to marry her himself, so that the old taboo would be broken by his own example. The hypocrites made of it what they could.

The same surah gives the Prophet’s ﷺ wives their choice between this world and Allah and His Messenger; names them the mothers of the believers; lays down the screen between them and visitors; and tells the believing women to draw their outer garments about them when they go out. And it gives the believers a command that is obeyed, somewhere, at every moment: “Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who believe, send blessings upon him, and greet him with peace.”

occasions.title: Zayd ibn Ḥārithah
occasions.text: “Zayd ibn Ḥārithah, the freedman of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ — we used to call him nothing but Zayd son of Muḥammad, until the Qurʾan came down: ‘Call them by their fathers; that is more just with Allah.’”
occasions.source: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar: al-Bukhārī (4782) and Muslim (2425).

occasions.title: Anas ibn al-Naḍr
occasions.text: Anas said: “We consider that this ayah came down about Anas ibn al-Naḍr: ‘Among the believers are men who have been true to what they pledged to Allah.’” He had missed Badr and vowed that if he saw another battle Allah would see what he would do; at Uḥud he went forward alone and was found with more than eighty wounds.
occasions.source: Anas ibn Mālik: al-Bukhārī (4783, 2805) and Muslim (1903).

occasions.title: The choice
occasions.text: ʿĀʾishah said that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was commanded to give his wives the choice, he began with her: “I am going to mention something to you; do not be hasty until you have consulted your parents.” Then he recited the two ayat. She said: “Is it about this that I should consult my parents? I want Allah, His Messenger and the home of the Hereafter.” And all his wives did as she did.

occasions.title: Zaynab bint Jaḥsh
occasions.text: Zayd came complaining, and the Prophet ﷺ kept saying: “Be mindful of Allah, and keep your wife.” Anas said: had the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concealed anything, he would have concealed this. Zaynab used to say to the other wives: “Your families gave you in marriage; Allah gave me in marriage from above seven heavens.”

occasions.title: The screen
occasions.text: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married Zaynab he invited the people to a meal. They ate and then sat on, talking, and he was too shy to tell them to leave. He rose; some left, and three stayed. When at last they had gone, Anas went to enter with him, and he let down the curtain between them — and the ayah of the screen was sent down. ʿUmar had earlier said: “Messenger of Allah, the good and the bad come in to you; if only you would order the mothers of the believers to be screened.”
occasions.source: Anas ibn Mālik: al-Bukhārī (4791, 4790) and Muslim (1428).

aim: It centres on Allah’s care for His Prophet ﷺ, and the protection of his honour and his household.
themes: The Messenger ﷺ as an example
Sending blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ

outline.title: The Prophet ﷺ, and false relationships
outline.summary: O Prophet, be mindful of Allah, and do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites. Allah has not put two hearts in any man’s breast; nor made your wives, whom you liken to your mothers’ backs, your mothers; nor made your adopted sons your sons. Call them by their fathers. The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves, and his wives are their mothers.

outline.title: The siege
outline.summary: O you who believe, remember Allah’s favour upon you when hosts came against you, and We sent against them a wind, and hosts you did not see. When they came at you from above you and from below, and eyes swerved and hearts reached the throats — there the believers were tried and shaken. The hypocrites said: “Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion.” A party of them said: “People of Yathrib, there is no stand for you here; go back.” Others asked leave: “Our houses are exposed” — and they were not exposed; they wanted only to flee.

outline.title: An excellent example
outline.summary: In the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent example, for whoever hopes in Allah and the Last Day (33:21). When the believers saw the confederates they said: “This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us” — and it only increased them in faith. Among the believers are men who have been true to what they pledged to Allah. Allah turned back the disbelievers in their rage; they gained no good. And He brought down from their strongholds those of the People of the Book who had backed them.

outline.title: The mothers of the believers
outline.summary: O Prophet, say to your wives: if you desire the life of this world and its adornment, come, I will provide for you and release you handsomely; but if you desire Allah and His Messenger and the home of the Hereafter, Allah has prepared a great reward. Wives of the Prophet, you are not like any other women. Remain in your houses; establish the prayer; obey Allah and His Messenger. — And for the men and women who submit, believe, obey, are truthful, patient, humble, give charity, fast, guard their chastity and remember Allah much: forgiveness, and a great reward.

outline.title: Zayd and Zaynab; the Seal of the Prophets
outline.summary: It is not for a believing man or woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, to have any choice in it. When Zayd had ended his marriage with her, We gave her to you in marriage, so that there should be no difficulty for the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons. Muḥammad is not the father of any of your men; he is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets.

outline.title: Remember Allah; the Prophet’s ﷺ marriages
outline.summary: O you who believe, remember Allah with much remembrance. O Prophet, We have sent you as a witness, a bringer of good news and a warner, one who calls to Allah by His leave, and a lamp spreading light. Then the rulings on a divorce before consummation, and on the women lawful to the Prophet ﷺ in particular.

outline.title: The screen, the blessing and the outer garment
outline.summary: O you who believe, do not enter the Prophet’s houses unless you are given leave; and when you ask his wives for anything, ask them from behind a screen. Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet: O you who believe, send blessings upon him and greet him with peace. O Prophet, tell your wives, your daughters and the women of the believers to draw their outer garments close about them. If the hypocrites and the rumour-mongers of Madinah do not desist, We shall set you upon them.

outline.title: The Hour, and the Trust
outline.summary: People ask you about the Hour. The Day their faces are turned in the Fire they will say: “If only we had obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger. Our Lord, we obeyed our masters and our great ones, and they led us astray.” O you who believe, be mindful of Allah and speak a word that is straight. We offered the Trust to the heavens, the earth and the mountains, and they declined to bear it and feared it; and man took it up.

keyAyah.why: Said in the middle of the siege, of a man digging beside his Companions. It is the Qurʾan’s warrant for following the Sunnah.

virtues.text: It was said: “Messenger of Allah, we know how to greet you with peace; but how do we send blessings upon you?” He said: “Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, as You sent blessings upon the family of Ibrāhīm; You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. O Allah, bless Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, as You blessed the family of Ibrāhīm; You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.”
virtues.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ

virtues.text: When the confederates had been driven off, the Prophet ﷺ said: “Now we shall raid them, and they will not raid us; we shall go to them.”

before: Al-Sajdah, the last of a long run of Makkan surahs, ended: turn from them, and wait. Al-Aḥzāb opens in Madinah, with the wait over and the enemy at the wall.
after: Al-Aḥzāb ends with the Trust that the heavens and the earth declined. Sabaʾ opens with praise of the One to whom everything in the heavens and the earth belongs.
